overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a cool, marine-influenced morning with temperatures locked in a very tight range of 62-63°F since midnight, with essentially zero warming velocity observed as of 08:00 ET. Patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies are suppressing early warming, consistent with a classic June Gloom pattern. The day is trending cooler than what NWP models initially suggested, with the current running max of just 63°F and no meaningful diurnal warming underway yet.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in reasonable agreement with each other — HRRR at 69.5°F, ECMWF at 68.2°F, and NBM at 67.0°F — but all three are projecting a substantial warming of 5-7°F from the current running max, which has not yet begun materializing. The intraday model is showing a much wider and flatter distribution (with notable probability mass spread from the upper 60s all the way into the upper 70s), suggesting considerable uncertainty about whether the marine layer will clear sufficiently to allow afternoon heating.
max_temp_prediction: Given the persistent marine layer, near-zero warming velocity as of mid-morning, and NWP model consensus clustering around 67-70°F, today's TMAX is most likely to land in the 67-70°F range if the fog clears mid-morning as forecast. The NWS official forecast of 69°F appears reasonable as a central estimate, though a cooler outcome in the 65-67°F range is plausible if cloud cover lingers longer than expected. Confidence is moderate-low due to the marine layer persistence and the intraday model's unusually flat/wide probability distribution.
